inputs.original_text: South Dakota Governor Larry Rhoden signed a bill on Thursday that requires new registered voters to prove that they are United States citizens in order to cast a ballot in state elections. In the press release, Senate Bill 175 was explained to: only appl[y] to state elections and only impacts new registrants. inputs.modified_text: Larry Rhoden has signed Senate Bill 175, adding paperwork hurdles for South Dakotans who want to vote. Those barriers hit people with fewer resources hardest, while the state shifts responsibility onto individuals instead of making participation accessible. This isn’t a neutral administrative tweak: it’s a choice to make political power harder to reach for people already facing inequality.
